name: Japan
tagline: A named minority route, on a calendar built for the people using it
summary: Japan's English-taught bachelor's degrees are a deliberate, named set built on top of the Japanese system, and the IB Diploma is one of the qualifications they were designed to receive. The University of Tokyo's PEAK closed after September 2026; its English-taught College of Design opens in September 2027 and names the IB first. Around it sit Waseda's six English-based schools, Keio's PEARL, Sophia, ICU, Kyoto's iUP, Tohoku's new Gateway College, APU and Akita. The Japanese year starts in April, so the September and October intakes exist mainly for international applicants — which is why they fit a May 2027 IB session, and why their deadlines run from October 2026 to April 2027, all before results.
whyConsider: The University of Tokyo opens its first new undergraduate faculty in about seventy years in September 2027, taught entirely in English, with half its hundred places on a route built for international qualifications and the IB named first.

Keio's PEARL runs three application periods for September 2027 entry, the last closing on 7 April 2027 and deciding on 24 May — the latest Japanese deadline on this page, and the only decision here that lands after the examination session.
Waseda takes one application for six English-based schools in a single winter window, which is unusually friendly against Japan's older October deadlines.

Kyoto's iUP asks for no Japanese at all: six months of intensive preparatory language teaching, then four years of undergraduate study, with admission and tuition fee waivers and monthly scholarships.

Money often comes with the offer rather than by separate application: Waseda decides its scholarships from the admission result, APU awards tuition reductions at admission, and Kyoto's iUP offers fee waivers and monthly scholarships.
Several programmes, ICU and Akita and APU among them, are built on a bilingual liberal-arts model that maps onto the Diploma's breadth.
watchOuts: PEAK has ended, and that is not the same as Todai closing. The College of Design's applications for September 2027 close on 5 November 2026, the earliest Japanese deadline recorded here, and it is a five-year integrated bachelor's and master's programme rather than a bachelor's degree.

Tohoku's FGL courses and Sophia's Green Science and Green Engineering courses took their last students in 2026. Tohoku's replacement, Gateway College, takes applications for October 2027 from 15 December 2026 to 14 January 2027.

April is the default intake and September is the exception. April 2027 entry would have meant applying in the middle of 2026 and is not realistic for this cohort; Kyoto's iUP enrols in October, which is a third calendar again.
There is no central portal, no shared calendar and no common application. Six months separate the earliest deadline from the latest, and each application carries its own fee.

MEXT is not a route into the English-taught sector. The undergraduate scholarship funds a preparatory year in Japanese followed by a degree taught in Japanese; English-medium study happens only through 'direct placement', which MEXT decides, and MEXT also chooses the university, with no objection allowed.

The MEXT undergraduate scholarship depends on your nationality: you apply through the Japanese embassy in your country of citizenship, and the embassy in Copenhagen does not offer it to Danish nationals. The Embassy of Japan in Copenhagen lists two MEXT types for Danish nationals — Japanese Studies and Research Student, both for students already at university. If you hold another nationality, check whether the Japanese embassy in that country offers the undergraduate type; otherwise plan around institutional awards, and ask the embassy in writing if MEXT matters to you.

The only official fee figure quoted here is the University of Tokyo's, and its page carries no price year. The fee table linked from Japan's official study-promotion site is drawn from the Student Guide to Japan 2019–2020.

Japanese universities generally want documents apostilled and sometimes notarised, and a Certificate of Eligibility must be obtained before the student visa. Neither fits inside a November deadline arranged in October.

ibRecognition.subjectLevelRule: There is no national rule. Each English-taught programme treats the full IB Diploma as meeting the twelve-year schooling condition and sets its own standard on top. The UTokyo College of Design is the one that publishes a number: it expects 38 of 42 points across the six subjects plus at least 2 for TOK and the Extended Essay, and says expectations 'are not cut off scores'. Keio's PEARL and Tohoku's Gateway College accept an IB Diploma or predicted grades.
ibRecognition.gradeConversion: No national conversion table. Each programme reads IB points directly.
notes: Predicted grades do the work. Every September or October 2027 decision recorded here is made before 6 July 2027. Keio and Tohoku accept predictions in so many words; the UTokyo College of Design accepts a certified predicted score from anyone whose exams fall after its deadline, makes the offer conditional, and wants final results by 16 August 2027.

Some programmes want SAT or ACT, or the Examination for Japanese University Admission for International Students, on top of the IB. The requirements are not uniform and have to be read programme by programme.

MEXT's scholarship route applies its own academic condition, and it depends on your nationality: you apply through the Japanese embassy in your country of citizenship. The Embassy of Japan in Denmark does not offer the undergraduate scholarship to Danish nationals; if you hold another nationality, check whether the embassy in that country does.

language.englishTaughtBachelors: A few dozen programmes nationally, named rather than general: the UTokyo College of Design from September 2027; Waseda's six English-based schools; Keio's PEARL and GIGA; Sophia's Faculty of Liberal Arts, Sustainable Futures programme and Digital Green Technology; ICU's bilingual liberal-arts degree; Tohoku's Gateway College; Kyushu's international programmes; Nagoya's G30; Tsukuba; Hokkaido; Kyoto's iUP; APU; and Akita International University. Temple University Japan awards an American degree in Tokyo. No national total is given here.
language.englishProof: Set per programme, usually as a test. The UTokyo College of Design and Tohoku's Gateway College both want TOEFL iBT 80, IELTS 6.0, Duolingo 110 or Cambridge 169 or more; Keio PEARL wants TOEFL iBT or IELTS Academic. Whether an IB English A or B result replaces the test is not confirmed at any of them, so ask.
notes: Kyoto's iUP states that no Japanese proficiency is required at the outset — the six-month preparatory course exists to build it.

No English-taught programme requires Japanese to enrol, and essentially all of them require you to study it. You will need it for part-time work, housing and daily life whatever your degree is taught in.
APU and ICU are formally bilingual: you take courses in both languages as your Japanese improves.
MEXT's undergraduate scholarship runs the other way. Its default is a year of preparatory Japanese followed by a degree taught in Japanese.

feeContext.summary: Japan charges the same tuition to every nationality, so there is no EU/non-EU split to look for. The structure is a one-off admission fee plus annual tuition, with private universities well above national ones and science and engineering above the humanities. Budget for the admission fee separately: it is charged once and it is substantial.
feeContext.typicalRange: The University of Tokyo publishes an admission fee of 282,000 yen once and tuition of 642,960 yen a year — above the 535,800 yen national standard, which is why a national figure should never be quoted for a particular university. It is the only official institutional figure quoted here.
feeContext.priceYear: Not stated on the source page, read 2026-09-23

livingContext.housing: Most English-taught programmes guarantee or strongly prioritise a first-year place in a university dormitory or international house, which is cheaper and far simpler than the private market. APU houses all first-year international students in AP House. Private renting in Japan involves key money, guarantor requirements and agency fees that are difficult to navigate from abroad — take the dormitory.
livingContext.healthcare: Enrolment in National Health Insurance is compulsory for anyone staying more than three months and is arranged at the municipal office when you register. It covers roughly 70 per cent of medical costs and students typically add the university's own supplementary cover. An EHIC does not apply.
livingContext.workRights: Students with College Student (留学) status may work up to 28 hours a week once they hold a blanket Permission to Engage in Activity Other Than That Permitted (Immigration Services Agency). Check the rules for longer hours in the official long vacations with your university.
livingContext.residency: EU citizenship changes nothing. The university applies for a Certificate of Eligibility once you accept an offer; you take it to the Embassy of Japan in Copenhagen for a Student visa. On arrival you receive a residence card, register at the municipal office within 14 days and enrol in National Health Insurance. Allow three months and expect documents to need an apostille.
funding: MEXT Undergraduate Scholarship, Embassy Recommendation: in the 2027 round, five years including a preparatory year in Japanese, 117,000 yen (about €650 at the ECB rate of 24 September 2026) a month, fees waived and air tickets paid, with MEXT choosing the university. The Embassy of Japan in Denmark does not offer this type to Danish nationals, so it is listed only because people ask about it.
University-recommendation MEXT places, under which a Japanese university nominates its own admitted students. The route exists; ask each admissions office whether it holds MEXT quota places.
JASSO Honors Scholarship, a monthly grant for privately financed international students. Check the current amount with JASSO.

Institutional awards decided at admission. Waseda states that its scholarship recipients are determined by the admission result with no separate application and that its awards are grants rather than loans; APU operates tuition-reduction scholarships at several levels; Kyoto's iUP offers admission and tuition fee waivers plus monthly scholarships.

funding.note: A full degree outside the EU/EEA follows separate rules, with its own ties-to-Denmark form: check su.dk before budgeting.

sectorLandscape.summary: Japan's official answer to what its higher education is made of names five kinds of institution international students may enter, and English-language guidance almost always stops at the first. Beyond the 大学 sit 短期大学 junior colleges, 高等専門学校 kōsen that take students at fifteen for a five-year technical programme, 専門学校 professional training colleges, and since 2019 the 専門職大学 professional and vocational universities. The English-taught undergraduate sector is not one of these categories: it is a named set of programmes inside the first one, on a September or October intake that the rest of the system does not use.

routes.what: Four years to a bachelor's degree, six for medicine, dentistry, veterinary medicine and pharmacy. National, local public and private, and the difference is largely money — the private universities charge considerably more and hold most of the English-taught provision. Every programme on this page sits here.
routes.note: The English-taught programmes inside this category are a named minority, admitted through their own rounds, on their own calendar, often at a different time of year from the Japanese-medium cohort at the same university.

routes.what: Two or three years ending in an associate degree rather than a bachelor's. Heavily weighted towards early-years and primary teaching, nursing and allied health, nutrition, home economics and design, and historically towards women students.
routes.note: Named because MEXT names it as one of the five routes open to international students. Whether any junior college admits an IB holder in practice, and in what language, is not known.

routes.what: A five-year engineering and technology programme entered at fifteen, straight from lower secondary, with a two-year advanced course on top. Fifty-one national kōsen plus local public and private ones. Graduates are hired by Japanese manufacturers in numbers out of all proportion to the sector's size.
routes.note: Listed because it has no European equivalent and is rarely mentioned in English-language advice. An IB Diploma holder is four years too late for the ordinary entry point; the advanced course and third-year transfer could in theory apply, so ask a kōsen directly.

routes.what: Post-secondary specialised training: two-year diploma courses of 62 credits or more and four-year advanced diploma courses of 124 or more, in animation and game design, IT, hospitality and cookery, fashion, care work, automotive engineering and dozens of other named trades.
routes.note: It is a large part of Japanese post-secondary education by student numbers, it enrols many international students, and it is rarely mentioned in English-language guidance for IB students. Only MEXT's own description of it is covered here.

routes.what: Created in 2019 to sit between the university and the professional training college: four years to a bachelor's degree (professional), or two to three years to an associate degree (professional), with a substantial compulsory placement built into the curriculum.
routes.note: The newest category in the Japanese system and the least documented in English. Listed so that the route is visible.

routes.englishName: Japan campus of a foreign university
routes.what: A foreign university operating in Japan and awarding its own home degree. Temple University, Japan Campus teaches entirely in English in Tokyo and allows transfer to Philadelphia.
routes.note: Useful if you want an American-style degree with a Japanese life around it, and priced accordingly — it charges American tuition, not Japanese.

notes: Audited 2026-09-24 (docs/research/audit/jp.md). Dates were read for the University of Tokyo, Keio, Waseda, Kyoto, Kyushu and Tohoku; the other institutions are listed with their programmes but their rounds were not read.
Re-check in November 2026, when Waseda is expected to publish its September 2027 window, and again in April 2027 for the MEXT 2028 guidelines.

Not established: any minimum IB score other than the UTokyo College of Design's stated expectation; most application fees; the JASSO Honors Scholarship amount; living costs from an official page; and the university-recommendation route into MEXT.
The Embassy of Japan in Denmark's pages refuse plain fetches (HTTP 403) but open in an ordinary browser; the Study in Japan page was read that way on 2026-09-24.
